intro.whisper: Is that the new math teacher?
intro.chair: Class, this is our math candidate. Our computer science students keep tripping on binary. {name}, could you explain it so it finally sticks?

intro.title: Editing for accuracy
intro.whisper: Is that the new English teacher?
intro.chair: Class, this is our English candidate. Brother Price has volunteered his write-up of the Kimball Building dedication. {name}, would you show us how to edit it for accuracy?
intro.verdict: Careful, kind and accurate. I'll recommend you to President Bednar.
intro.thanks: Thank you — and thanks, Brother Price, for being a good sport.

You never have to look at the picture

intro.title: Drawing what you see
intro.chair: Class, meet our art candidate. Our students struggle to draw what they actually see. {name}, can you show them how? If that old projector cooperates.
intro.verdict: Even with the projector dying, you kept the class drawing. I'll recommend you to President Bednar.
intro.thanks: Thank you! Someone should look at that projector, though.
intro.frame: Let's try the grid method. I'll project a picture, and we'll copy it one square at a time. Today's picture: my vision of a temple on the hill.

intro.title: Projector repair
intro.whisper: Hey — isn't that the Spori's projector?
intro.chair: Class, this is our engineering candidate. Physical Plant just brought us the Spori's projector; it shorted out during the art demo. {name}, can you fix it and explain what went wrong?
intro.verdict: Fixed it live, and they understood why. I'll recommend you to President Bednar.
intro.thanks: Thank you! Tell the art studio their projector is ready.
intro.frame: Sure. A projector is just a few circuits. Let's lay its wiring out on the pegboard and follow the path the power takes.
